chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ja'far al-Ahowl, from Abu Ubaydah al-Hadda', who said:

I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying while he was in prostration: 'I ask You by the right of Your beloved Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family), that You exchange my bad deeds for good ones, and reckon me with an easy reckoning.'

Then he said during the second (prostration): 'I ask You by the right of Your beloved Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family), that You suffice me with the provisions of the world and every terror before Paradise.'

And he said during the third: 'I ask You by the right of Your beloved Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family), since You have forgiven me the many sins and the few, and accepted from me my slight deeds.'

Then he said during the fourth: 'I ask You by the right of Your beloved Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family), since You have brought me into Paradise and made me from its dwellers, and since You have saved me from the blasts of the Fire by Your mercy. And may Allah bless Muhammad and his family.'

key_terms.بَدَّلْتَ سَيِّئَاتِي حَسَنَاتٍ: Exchange my bad deeds for good ones
key_terms.حَقِّ حَبِيبِكَ: The right of Your beloved (referring to Prophet Muhammad)
key_terms.حِسَاباً يَسِيراً: An easy reckoning (on the Day of Judgment)

ai.seo_question: What are the specific supplications recited during the four prostrations in Shia prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the Shia practice of invoking the 'Haqq' (right/authority) of the Prophet Muhammad as a means of intercession during the intimate moments of prostration. It reflects the theological concept of *Tawassul* through the Ahl al-Bayt, where the supplicant asks Allah to transform sins into good deeds and grant ease in the Hereafter based on the Prophet's merit. The structure emphasizes a progressive spiritual journey from forgiveness to ultimate salvation, rooted in divine mercy.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, and Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Al Hassan Bin Mahboub, from Abu Ja’far Al Ahowl, from Abu Ubeyda Al Haza’a who said,
‘I heard Abu Ja’farasws saying while heasws was in Sajdah: ‘I ask Youazwj by the right of Yourazwj Beloved Muhammadsaww to Exchange my (Shias’) sins to Rewards and Reckon me with an easy Reckoning’.
Then heasws said during the second (Sajdah): ‘I ask Youazwj by the right of Yourazwj Beloved Muhammadsaww to Suffice me with the provisions of the world and (from) every horror before the Paradise’.

And he<sup>asws</sup> said during the third: ‘I ask You<sup>azwj</sup> by the right of Your<sup>azwj</sup> Beloved Muhammad<sup>saww</sup> to Forgive the numerous of the sins of my (Shias) and the little ones, and Accept from me my deeds easily’.

Then he<sup>asws</sup> said during the fourth: ‘I ask You<sup>azwj</sup> by the right of Your<sup>azwj</sup> Muhammad<sup>saww</sup> to Enter me into the Paradise, and Make me to be from its dwellers, and Rescue my (Shias) from the blasts of the Fire by Your<sup>azwj</sup> Mercy. And Blessings of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> be upon Muhammad<sup>saww</sup> and his<sup>saww</sup> Progeny<sup>asws</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from al-Hassan ibn Mahbub from, abu Ja‘far al-Ahwal from abu ‘Ubaydah al-Hadhdha’ who has said the following:

“I heard abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, say when prostrating, ‘(O Lord,) I plead before You through the right of Muhammad, Your beloved one, to change my bad deeds to good ones and hold my accountability very little.
In the second prostration said, ‘(O Lord,) I plead before You through the right of Muhammad, Your beloved one, to suffice me in (my) needs in this world and all frightening matters up to paradise.

In the third sajdah said, ‘(O Lord,) I plead before You through the right of Muhammad, Your beloved one, to forgive my sins, be it a great deal or a smaller amount and accept my very few (good deeds).

In the fourth sajdah he said, ‘(O Lord,) I plead before You through the right of Muhammad, Your beloved one, to admit me in paradise, make me of its dwellers, save me from the effect of fire through Your mercy, and, O Allah, grant Muhammad and his family a compensation worthy of their serving Your cause.”
